processing: Darjeeling tea from mostly China bushes, made as first flush and other black lots, with oolong and small white lots as well. The garden is gradually moving toward organic practices.
harvest_season: Spring Chinary and first flush lots are the ones most seen; later flushes follow as elsewhere in Darjeeling.
appearance_dry: Typically olive to brown twisted leaf with some pale tips in spring lots.
appearance_liquor: Clear amber in black lots, paler in spring.
appearance_wet: Mixed green and copper leaf, as is usual for China-bush Darjeeling.
taste_profile: A sweet, floral scent over a clear cup is the one tasting account on record; expect the familiar Darjeeling mix of flowers and light fruit.

brewing.notes: Western-style. China-bush spring lots stay sweeter in water a little off the boil.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush, often as a spring Chinary. As with other Darjeelings, current-season lots are the norm and spring tea fades fastest.
description:
Mim is a small-profile garden at Jorebunglow near Sukhiapokhari, about 21 km from Darjeeling town. Its height is given anywhere from about 1,500 to 2,000 metres, and it mainly grows China bushes.

The range is broader than you might expect, with first flush, oolong and some rare white lots alongside regular black tea. It is also said to be run by the Government of India through the Andrew Yule Company, which would make it unique in Darjeeling, though that is not widely confirmed.

One taster describes a clear amber cup with a sweet, floral scent. Typical of China-bush Darjeeling, that is a fair starting expectation, and water a little under the boil suits it.

Copy on shop pages for this garden tends to be recycled, so do not lean on it. Look for a clear year and flush, and judge by the cup.
history: Little about the garden is firmly documented. It is dated loosely to the mid-1800s, with some claims reaching as early as 1832. Local tradition derives the name from "Mem", a word for a British woman, saying the place was called "Mem ko Kaman" while one ran it; this is a story and not a record.
